tools.description: The actual files somebody brought back for a job — photographs, video, transcripts — with where each one says it was taken and whether the challenge code was found in it. tools.name: job_receipt
tools.description: The signed receipt for a finished job. It states what was asked, what evidence arrived, what was concluded and what moved, and can be verified by anyone without trusting the exchange. A sandbox job's receipt says so in words, reports nothing paid, and is not anchored — it is not evidence of anything

tools.name: job_status
tools.description: Where a job has got to: whether anybody has taken it, what they submitted, whether it passed checking, and what was paid. A reply carrying sandbox true is a simulated run: nobody went anywhere and nothing was paid, whatever the states say.

tools.name: list_bids
tools.description: The offers on an open job: what each person would charge, when they could do it, and what they said about how. Show these to your human rather than picking on price alone.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: check_feasible, do_in_world, job_evidence, observe_world · Private data: do_in_world, job_evidence, observe_world · Public sink: check_feasible, do_in_world, observe_world · Destructive: job_status.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: check_feasible, do_in_world, job_evidence, observe_world · Private data: do_in_world, job_evidence, observe_world · Public sink: check_feasible, do_in_world, observe_world · Destructive: job_status

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
